candidate.answerReason: Evaluation at 1 gives the total coefficient sum 3^n, and evaluation at -1 gives the even coefficient sum minus the odd coefficient sum as 1.

methods.label: Separate even and odd coefficients by evaluation
methods.explanation:
Substituting \(x=1\) adds all the coefficients, while substituting \(x=-1\) changes the signs of precisely the odd-power terms. These two evaluations separate the sum we want.

Let \(t\) be the sum of the odd-power coefficients. Substituting \(x=1\) gives
\[
s+t=(1+1+1)^n=3^n.
\]
At \(x=-1\), every even power is \(1\) and every odd power is \(-1\), so
\[
s-t=(1-1+1)^n=1.
\]
Adding the equations cancels \(t\), giving
\[
2s=3^n+1,
\qquad \boxed{s=\frac{3^n+1}{2}}.
\]
The argument also covers \(n=0\), when the odd-power sum is empty and equals zero. The answer is choice \(\boxed{E}\).
methods.levelReason: Polynomial evaluation at 1 and -1 and addition of two equations require only elementary algebra.
